hints: Focus on what makes a carbon chiral, a carbon attached to four completely different atoms or groups.
Look first at the left-hand carbon carrying the $\text{NH}_2$ group, check its four bonds to $\text{H}$, $\text{NH}_2$, $\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ and $\text{C=O}$.
Now do the same test for the carbon on the right carrying the $\text{NH}$ group, then quickly rule out $\text{C=O}$, $\text{CH}_2$ and $\text{CH}_3$ carbons to finish the count.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for chirality**

A chiral carbon is $sp^3$ tetrahedral and bonded to four different groups. If even two groups are the same, it cannot be chiral.

Rule to apply:
$$\text{chiral C = C with 4 different substituents}$$

**Check the left centre (aspartic acid part)**

Find the carbon bonded to $\text{NH}_2$. Its four groups are $\text{H}$, $\text{NH}_2$, $\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ and $\text{CONH}$. All four are different, so this carbon is chiral. Well done for spotting the first one.

**Check the right centre (phenylalanine part)**

Find the carbon bonded to $\text{NH}$. Its four groups are $\text{H}$, $\text{NHCO}$, $\text{CH}_2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$ and $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$. All four are different, so this carbon is also chiral. That gives us two so far.

**Rule out all the other carbons**

Carbonyl $\text{C=O}$ carbons have only three groups, $\text{CH}_2$ carbons have two H atoms, $\text{CH}_3$ has three H atoms, and the $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$ ring has no chiral carbon as stated. So no more chiral centres exist, and the total is 2.

options.A: Only counting one centre is incomplete. Students who choose 1 often find the left $\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)$ centre but miss the very similar right $\text{CH}(\text{NH})$ centre.
options.B: Correct. There are exactly 2 chiral carbons: the $\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)$ carbon on the left and the $\text{CH}(\text{NH})$ carbon on the right. Each has four different groups attached.
options.C: There is no third chiral centre. Students who choose 3 often mistakenly count a $\text{CH}_2$ group next to a carbonyl or phenyl ring, but a $\text{CH}_2$ has two identical H atoms so it can never be chiral.
options.D: Far too many. Students who choose 4 often count carbonyl carbons or the $\text{OCH}_3$ carbon. Carbonyl C is planar with only three attachments and $\text{CH}_3$ has three identical H atoms, so neither can be chiral.
